2026-08-20T03:25:39.0058975Z ## MCP Servers Mounted as Shell CLI Commands
2026-08-20T03:25:39.0059698Z 
2026-08-20T03:25:39.0060308Z The following servers are available as CLI commands on `PATH`:
2026-08-20T03:25:39.0061209Z 
2026-08-20T03:25:39.0061886Z - `safeoutputs` — run `safeoutputs --help` to see available tools
2026-08-20T03:25:39.0062826Z 
2026-08-20T03:25:39.0065700Z > **IMPORTANT**: For `safeoutputs` and `mcpscripts`, **always use the CLI commands** listed above instead of the equivalent MCP tools. The CLI wrappers are the preferred interface — do **not** call their MCP tools directly even though they may appear in your tool list.
2026-08-20T03:25:39.0069211Z >
2026-08-20T03:25:39.0073709Z > For `safeoutputs`, treat every successful command as a real write-intent declaration. Do **not** use `safeoutputs` for exploratory probing, auth checks, placeholder payloads, repeated "try again" variants, or manual runtime experiments. When you need a safe-output, emit the final intended call once. If you are not ready to perform the real action, use `noop` or `report_incomplete` instead.
2026-08-20T03:25:39.0078599Z >
2026-08-20T03:25:39.0080108Z > For all other servers listed here, they are **only** available as CLI commands and are **not** available as MCP tools.
2026-08-20T03:25:39.0081570Z 
2026-08-20T03:25:39.0081900Z ### How to Use
2026-08-20T03:25:39.0082338Z 
2026-08-20T03:25:39.0083503Z Each server is a standalone executable on your `PATH`. Invoke it from bash like any other shell command:
2026-08-20T03:25:39.0084860Z 
2026-08-20T03:25:39.0085189Z ```bash
2026-08-20T03:25:39.0086139Z # Call a tool — pass arguments as --name value pairs
2026-08-20T03:25:39.0087473Z <server-name> <tool-name> --param1 value1 --param2 value2
2026-08-20T03:25:39.0088833Z ```
2026-08-20T03:25:39.0089231Z 
2026-08-20T03:25:39.0089684Z **Example** — using the `playwright` CLI:
2026-08-20T03:25:39.0090701Z ```bash
2026-08-20T03:25:39.0091721Z playwright --help                                  # list all browser tools
2026-08-20T03:25:39.0093212Z playwright browser_navigate --url https://example.com
2026-08-20T03:25:39.0094794Z playwright browser_snapshot                        # capture page accessibility tree
2026-08-20T03:25:39.0096200Z ```
2026-08-20T03:25:39.0096589Z 
2026-08-20T03:25:39.0097667Z **Example** — using the `safeoutputs` CLI (safe outputs) when you are ready to emit the final real action:
2026-08-20T03:25:39.0099504Z ```bash
2026-08-20T03:25:39.0100561Z safeoutputs add_comment --issue_number 42 --body "Analysis complete"
2026-08-20T03:25:39.0101869Z ```
2026-08-20T03:25:39.0102261Z 
2026-08-20T03:25:39.0102973Z **Example** — using the `mcpscripts` CLI (mcp-scripts):
2026-08-20T03:25:39.0104091Z ```bash
2026-08-20T03:25:39.0105095Z mcpscripts --help                                  # list all script tools
2026-08-20T03:25:39.0138719Z mcpscripts mcpscripts-gh --args "pr list --repo owner/repo --limit 5"
2026-08-20T03:25:39.0140271Z ```
2026-08-20T03:25:39.0140677Z 
2026-08-20T03:25:39.0141191Z ### Passing Multiple or Complex Arguments (Preferred)
2026-08-20T03:25:39.0142003Z 
2026-08-20T03:25:39.0144763Z **Preferred approach for any tool call with multiple or complex arguments**: supply a JSON object on stdin using `.` as the sentinel. The bridge parses stdin as the argument object, preserving all native types (numbers, booleans, arrays) without shell-quoting issues.
2026-08-20T03:25:39.0147877Z 
2026-08-20T03:25:39.0148208Z ```bash
2026-08-20T03:25:39.0149247Z # Full argument payload as JSON via printf pipe
2026-08-20T03:25:39.0150837Z printf '{"issue_number":42,"body":"### Title\n\nBody paragraph one.\n\nBody paragraph two."}' \
2026-08-20T03:25:39.0152420Z   | safeoutputs add_comment .
2026-08-20T03:25:39.0153014Z 
2026-08-20T03:25:39.0153907Z # Works with any tool — just match the parameter names from <server> <tool> --help
2026-08-20T03:25:39.0155843Z printf '{"title":"Fix: something","body":"Details here","labels":["bug","priority-high"]}' \
2026-08-20T03:25:39.0157509Z   | safeoutputs create_issue .
2026-08-20T03:25:39.0158586Z ```
2026-08-20T03:25:39.0158994Z 
2026-08-20T03:25:39.0160425Z **When pipes are blocked by the bash security policy**, write the payload to a file first and use **file redirection** with the `.` sentinel instead:
2026-08-20T03:25:39.0162195Z 
2026-08-20T03:25:39.0162518Z ```bash
2026-08-20T03:25:39.0163752Z # Step 1 — write the JSON payload to a file using the Write tool or a bash heredoc
2026-08-20T03:25:39.0165438Z # Step 2 — redirect the file into the CLI command using '<'
2026-08-20T03:25:39.0166852Z safeoutputs create_pull_request . < /tmp/payload.json
2026-08-20T03:25:39.0167730Z 
2026-08-20T03:25:39.0168688Z # This is equivalent to piping but does not require a separate command before '|'
2026-08-20T03:25:39.0170320Z safeoutputs add_comment . < /tmp/comment.json
2026-08-20T03:25:39.0171448Z ```
2026-08-20T03:25:39.0171872Z 
2026-08-20T03:25:39.0172307Z > **Why prefer JSON payload mode?**
2026-08-20T03:25:39.0237590Z > - Single operation for any number of arguments — no repeated `--key value` flags
2026-08-20T03:25:39.0239862Z > - Native types (integers, booleans, arrays) are preserved exactly as specified
2026-08-20T03:25:39.0241716Z > - No shell quoting or escaping needed for newlines, quotes, or special characters
2026-08-20T03:25:39.0243648Z > - Agents can construct the payload as a structured object before emitting the command
2026-08-20T03:25:39.0245669Z > - File redirection (`< file`) works even when pipes (`|`) are restricted
2026-08-20T03:25:39.0246801Z 
2026-08-20T03:25:39.0247141Z ### Notes
2026-08-20T03:25:39.0247546Z 
2026-08-20T03:25:39.0248940Z - **Prefer JSON payload mode** (`. < file` or `printf '{...}' | server tool .`) for any call with multiple arguments or complex values
2026-08-20T03:25:39.0253053Z - All parameters can also be passed as `--name value` pairs; boolean flags can be set with `--flag` (no value) to mean `true`
2026-08-20T03:25:39.0255785Z - Use `.` as the only argument to parse stdin as a JSON object (all parameters supplied at once)
2026-08-20T03:25:39.0258658Z - Parameter names with hyphens or underscores are interchangeable (e.g. `issue-number` and `issue_number` both work)
2026-08-20T03:25:39.0260991Z - Output is printed to stdout; errors are printed to stderr with a non-zero exit code
2026-08-20T03:25:39.0268959Z - Run the CLI commands inside a `bash` tool call — they are shell executables, not MCP tools
2026-08-20T03:25:39.0280093Z - These CLI commands are read-only and cannot be modified by the agent
2026-08-20T03:25:39.0281466Z </mcp-clis>
2026-08-20T03:25:39.0282221Z <github-context>
